stem:
Yash says a whole number leaves remainder 3 when divided by 5. He writes numbers of that kind as $5k+3$ with whole number $k$, and keeps the remainder strictly between 0 and 4.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Every such number may also be written as $5k+5$, because remainder size does not matter.
The divisor 5 is produced by the remainder 3, rather than 5 and $k$ producing remainder 3.
Numbers leaving remainder 3 on division by 5 are exactly those of the form $5k+3$ with $0\le3<5$.
The same $5k+3$ form also covers numbers that leave remainder 4 when divided by 5.

teacher.key_rationale: Remainder form needs 0 ≤ r < divisor, so remainder 3 on division by 5 is 5k+3. Writing 5k+5 drops the remainder bound. Saying the remainder produces the divisor reverses the relation. Extending 5k+3 to remainder 4 over-extends the form.
